mn58:3.18: In the same way, prince, when you put this dilemma to him, the Buddha won’t be able to either spit it out or swallow it down.”
mn58:6.8: ‘Come, prince, refute the ascetic Gotama’s doctrine.
mn58:6.9: Then you will get a good reputation—
mn58:6.10: Prince Abhaya refuted the doctrine of the ascetic Gotama, so mighty and powerful!’
mn58:6.11: When he had spoken, sir, I said to the Jain Ñātika:
mn58:6.12: ‘But sir, how am I to refute the doctrine of the ascetic Gotama, so mighty and powerful?’
mn58:6.13: ‘Here, prince, go to the ascetic Gotama and say to him:
mn58:6.14: “Sir, may the Realized One utter speech that is disliked by others?”
mn58:6.15: When he’s asked this, if he answers:
mn58:6.16: “He may, prince,” say this to him:
mn58:6.17: “So what then, sir, is the difference between you and an ordinary person?
mn58:6.18: For even an ordinary person may utter speech that is disliked by others.”
mn58:6.20: “He may not, prince,” say this to him—
mn58:6.21: So why then, sir, did you declare of Devadatta:
mn58:6.22: “Devadatta is going to a place of loss, to hell, there to remain for an eon, irredeemable”?
mn58:6.23: Devadatta was angry and upset with what you said.’
mn58:6.24: When you put this dilemma to him, the Buddha won’t be able to either spit it out or swallow it down.
mn58:6.25: He’ll be like a man with an iron cross stuck in his throat, unable to either spit it out or swallow it down.
mn58:6.26: In the same way, prince, when you put this dilemma to him, the Buddha won’t be able to either spit it out or swallow it down.”
mn58:12.4: With Prince Abhaya is finished—the eighth.
